title: Check $$k=0$$
text: Start with $$k=0.$$ When $$k=0$$, $$\theta=\frac{4\pi}{3}.$$ This is within the interval $$[-2\pi$$, $$2\pi].$$

title: Check positive integers
text: Try $$k=1.$$ When $$k=1$$, $$\theta=\frac{4\pi}{3}+2\pi=\frac{10\pi}{3}.$$ This is outside our boundary of $$2\pi, $$ so we can stop checking positive integers.

title: Check negative integers
text: Now try $$k=-1.$$ When $$k=-1, $$ $$\theta=\frac{4\pi}{3}-2\pi=\frac{4\pi}{3}-\frac{6\pi}{3}=\frac{-2\pi}{3}.$$ This is greater than $$-2\pi, $$ so it is safely within our interval.

title: Check the next negative
text: Try $$k=-2.$$ $$\theta=\frac{4\pi}{3}-4\pi=\frac{-8\pi}{3}.$$ This is less than $$-2\pi, $$ so it falls outside our boundary. We can stop checking negative integers.

title: Compile the list
text: The only angles generated by our formula that fall inside the interval are $$\frac{4\pi}{3}$$ and $$\frac{-2\pi}{3}.$$
